# Actual convolution selectors, unequal dilations, and exact ambient-cap identities

The ordinary reflection correlation, its intrinsic parity master identity,
its moments, and attainment are already proved in
`candidate 93cf42ea22bcd767`.
This note does not claim those results anew. It gives an exact actual
counterexample to selecting a correlation maximizer, and then derives
the unequal-weight cap identity and the associated lattice obstruction.
These are auxiliary results, not counterexamples to OC.

## 1. A unique ordinary convolution maximizer below the Grünbaum target

Let

    K={(s,t):0<=t<=1, |s|<=(1+t)/2} in R^2.

This is a convex trapezoid of area M_K=3/2. For c=(xi,eta) in K let

    R_K(c)=|K intersect(2c-K)|.

At height t the original horizontal interval is centered at zero and
has length1+t. The reflected interval is centered at2xi and has length
1+2eta-t. Both are present exactly when

    max(0,2eta-1)<=t<=min(1,2eta).

The overlap of two intervals of fixed lengths is maximized when their
centers agree. Therefore R_K(xi,eta)<=R_K(0,eta). At xi=0 their
intersection has the smaller length. Integrating separately below and
above the symmetry height eta gives exactly

    R_K(0,eta)=2eta+eta^2                 if0<=eta<=1/2,
              1+2eta-3eta^2             if1/2<=eta<=1. (1)

The first polynomial is strictly increasing; the second has derivative
2-6eta<0 on[1/2,1]. Thus the unique maximizing vertical coordinate is
eta=1/2, where R_K=5/4. At that height any nonzero xi strictly lowers
the overlap: near t=1/2 the two interval lengths are arbitrarily close,
while their centers have fixed positive distance2|xi|. On a positive
length interval of heights, neither smaller interval is then contained
in the larger, or the intervals are disjoint. In either case their
intersection is strictly smaller than the smaller length. Consequently

    c_*=(0,1/2) is the UNIQUE maximum of R_K,
    R_K(c_*)=5/4.                                      (2)

The retained intersection is centrally symmetric about c_*. Every
closed halfspace containing c_* therefore captures at least half its
area, namely5/8. The horizontal halfspace t<=1/2 captures exactly

    integral_0^(1/2)(1+t)dt=5/8

from the ORIGINAL K. Its raw depth is therefore exactly5/8, and

    depth_K(c_*)=5/12<4/9=Gamma_2.                      (3)

This proves failure of the optimizing-center selector itself, rather
than merely a weakness in a lower estimate for that selected center.
The original body still satisfies ordinary Grünbaum at its centroid.

## 2. The same failure for every number of integer variables

For any n>=0 take the actual convex body

    C=[0,1]^n times K,
    S={0,1}^n times K,     M=2^n(3/2).

For p in{0,1}^n, a pair z,w in that same binary cube satisfies
z+w=2p only when z=w=p, coordinate by coordinate. Hence the actual
mixed reflection correlation is exactly

    R_S(p,x)=R_K(x).

All its maximizing actual points are(p,c_*). At any such point, every
containing ambient halfspace captures at least5/8 from its own fiber,
because its trace there is a containing continuous halfspace or the
whole fiber. For the reverse bound put

    ell_p(z)=sum_j(2p_j-1)(z_j-p_j).

It is zero at p and at most-1 at every other binary base. The genuine
closed AMBIENT halfspace

    ell_p(z)+1/2-t>=0

captures precisely the downward cap t<=1/2 on base p and no other
fiber, since1/2-t<=1/2 throughout K. Therefore every actual reflection
maximizer has exact depth

    5/(12 times2^n)<Gamma_2/2^n.                        (4)

For n=0 the integer sum is empty and this is the preceding ordinary
example. All fibers have full continuous dimension two. No point is
rounded, no projection integral replaces a fiber sum, and the upper
certificate includes its required coupled integer/continuous normal.

## 3. Unequal dilations: one exact equation for every ambient halfspace

Now return to an arbitrary nonempty induced mixed set S of a compact
convex body. Put q=dim_H S, mu=H_q restricted to S, and let Y be an
ACTUAL point of S. For0<t<1 define the scaled intersection

    L_t(Y)=t(S-Y) intersect[-(1-t)(S-Y)],
    G_t(Y)=H_q(L_t(Y)),
    A_t(Y)=Y+L_t(Y)/t subset S,
    B_t(Y)=Y-L_t(Y)/(1-t) subset S.

These auxiliary scaled sets need not belong to the mixed lattice;
the two displayed endpoint sets do. Euclidean homotheties scale their
intrinsic q-measures by exactly t^q and(1-t)^q, including q=0 with
factor one. Let H={W:a.(W-Y)>=0} be ANY through-Y closed ambient
halfspace, with a nonzero full ambient normal. For Z in L_t(Y), its
paired endpoint signs are a.Z/t and-a.Z/(1-t). Thus their indicators
sum to1+1_{a.Z=0}. Integrating this pointwise identity gives EXACTLY

    t^q mu(A_t intersect H)+(1-t)^q mu(B_t intersect H)
       =G_t(Y)+H_q(L_t(Y) intersect{a.Z=0}).             (5)

This equation handles oblique and purely integer normals, and retains
all boundary mass. Since both endpoint sets are subsets of S, it gives

    mu(S intersect H)>=G_t(Y)/[t^q+(1-t)^q].            (6)

For a closed halfspace merely containing Y, its parallel through-Y
halfspace is a subset, so the same lower bound holds. At t=1/2,
L_t=(S intersect(2Y-S)-Y)/2 and G_t=2^(-q)R_S(Y); equation(6) then
reduces to the familiar R_S(Y)/2 certificate. The normalization G_t
must not be confused with the unscaled reflected intersection.

For a SINGLE full q-dimensional convex fiber with q>=1, this entire
unequal-weight certificate is no stronger than its balanced member.
Indeed the ordinary balanced-opposite-dilation lemma gives
G_t(Y)<=G_(1/2)(Y): the reflection of L_t is L_(1-t), and their
Minkowski midpoint lies in L_(1/2). BM proves the volume inequality.
If Y is on the fiber boundary, all these q-volumes are zero; otherwise
the intersections have nonempty relative interior, so the ordinary BM
argument applies directly. Power convexity gives

    t^q+(1-t)^q>=2^(1-q).

Consequently

    G_t(Y)/[t^q+(1-t)^q]<=R_S(Y)/2.                     (7)

For the binary product in Section2, unequal convex averages of distinct
binary bases cannot be an integer binary base. Hence only the own-fiber
term contributes for EVERY t in(0,1), and the same domination applies.
Optimizing the entire family of certificates(6) therefore still selects
the trapezoid's bad reflection center, with optimal certified raw mass
5/8. This excludes this specific unequal-weight repair of the selector.

## 4. Rational weights keep an exact congruence and Jacobian

Assume first t=r/(r+s) with positive coprime integers r,s, and let
m=r+s. Write Y=(p,x), p integer. At the fiber level,

    G_t(p,x)=sum_(rz+sw=mp)
                  H_q[tK_z intersect(x-(1-t)K_w)].     (8)

Here each summand is in the continuous affine q-space of that pair;
if the intersection is lower dimensional it has zero H_q measure.
There is one term for each ordered pair. The integer equation is
EXACTLY equivalent to

    z=p+s ell,  w=p-r ell,   ell in Z^n,

or, for the endpoint pair, to z congruent w modulo m. Coprimality
proves this coordinate by coordinate.

Only top-dimensional positive fibers contribute to(8). For such a
pair, convexity places tK_z+(1-t)K_w inside K_p. Its affine direction
is the sum of the two q-dimensional directions. Since q is the maximum
integer-fiber dimension, those directions must coincide, and K_p is
also positive q-dimensional in the same affine space. This is the
weighted counterpart of the archived midpoint alignment argument; it
does not assume all parity or residue classes have common directions.

Let mu_c be the original measure restricted to top-dimensional bases
in residue class c modulo m. For every nonnegative Borel Phi, or bounded
signed Borel Phi, the precise master identity is

    integral_S Phi(Y)G_t(Y)dmu(Y)
      =[t(1-t)]^q sum_(c modulo m) integral integral
             Phi(tA+(1-t)B)dmu_c(A)dmu_c(B).            (9)

For one aligned pair, the summand in(8) is the convolution of the
indicators of tK_z and(1-t)K_w, evaluated at x. Its support is their
Minkowski sum, contained in K_p. In orthonormal coordinates of their
common q-space, changing variables to the two ORIGINAL endpoints
has Jacobian t^q(1-t)^q. Tonelli then proves(9), and the finite sum
finishes the argument. For q=0 this is a finite ordered-pair count
with Jacobian one. In particular

    integral_S G_t dmu=[t(1-t)]^q sum_c M_c^2,
    integral_S Y G_t(Y)dmu(Y)=[t(1-t)]^q sum_c M_c m_c,

where M_c=mu_c(S) and m_c=integral A dmu_c(A).
These are not the original parity weights unless m=2.
The unscaled alternative K_z intersect[(x-(1-t)K_w)/t] has a different
Jacobian: its integral is(1-t)^q times the endpoint product mass.
Equation(9) consistently uses the SCALED normalization(8).

## 5. Actual lattice indexing produces isolated nonself parameter terms

Let P be the finite set of positive q-dimensional bases and let

    D=max_(z,w in P) ||z-w||_infinity,

with D=0 if P has only one base. If an irrational t admits integer
p=t z+(1-t)w, then z=w=p: any nonzero coordinate of z-w would express
t as a ratio of integers. For rational t=r/m in lowest terms, a
nonself pair satisfies z-w=m ell with ell nonzero, hence m<=D.
There are only finitely many reduced rational numbers in(0,1) with
such a denominator. Thus every nonself contribution to G_t at any
actual integer center occurs at one of finitely many rational t.
For fixed S, in a punctured neighborhood of t=1/2 avoiding those
finitely many values, only the own-fiber term remains. This is not a
continuous variation of the original parity sum.

An exact example makes the discontinuity explicit. Take n=1 and
C=[-1,1] times K, where K is any full d-dimensional centrally symmetric
convex body centered at zero; take Y=(0,0). The only integer fibers
are-1,0,1, all equal to K. If t!=1/2, only the pair(0,0) has weighted
integer center zero, and symmetry gives

    G_t(Y)=min(t,1-t)^d |K|.

At t=1/2 there are the THREE ordered pairs(-1,1),(0,0),(1,-1), so

    G_(1/2)(Y)=3 times2^(-d)|K|.                       (10)

The limiting value from other weights is only2^(-d)|K|. This is an
actual convex body with complete integer fibers, not an arbitrary
sampled array. It refutes a continuous-parameter first-variation step
that keeps all nonself parity terms while insisting on actual integer
centers. It does not preclude a different variation that explicitly
changes the indexing or tracks its discrete jumps.

## Scope

Equation(5) is the new exact all-halfspace relation, and(9)--(10) keep
unequal-weight lattice indexing and normalization explicit. The older
midpoint correlation and moment theorems are not being promoted anew.
The trapezoid is a certified failure of these optimizing selectors,
while OC remains valid there at other actual points. No conclusion
about arbitrary alternative center constructions follows.
